properties.description:
`detect_gaps` raises `published_surface_carries_no_intent` when a design declares at least one `published` or `both` Interface and marks not one Requirement `published`.

⭐ THE THIRD LEG. `cap:publish-surface` is VERIFIED and `req:publishable-promise` is ACCEPTED — "a published surface must be able to carry a behavioural promise, not only structure". The vocabulary existed and the tool existed. Nothing anywhere NOTICED that nobody had used them, which is the standing shape: vocabulary reaches a design only with a typed tool, an instruction, AND a detector that notices absence.

WHAT IT MEASURED ON ITS OWN DESIGN, 2026-09-22: reflow2 held 262 Requirements with 0 published and 3 published Interfaces, and flo2 — a real consumer that had mirrored it correctly — held 22 nodes with zero Requirements, Capabilities or Decisions among them, reachable from flo2's own design through a single edge.

TWO SILENCES, BOTH DELIBERATE. Silent when NOTHING is published: a design with no published boundary has no consumer and owes nobody a promise, and asking every private design would fire on nearly all of them. Silent at ONE: it fires on zero and never on "too few", because how many promises a design owes is not something a detector can know, and `set_requirement_designation` is explicit that publishing is a commitment the owner makes.

`both` counts as published: such a boundary consumes a contract and re-offers it onward, so a consumer relies on it exactly as much.
properties.name: A design that publishes contracts and publishes no promise is asked about it, once
